questions.prompt: What does MULTI/EXEC guarantee about the queued commands?

options.text: They roll back entirely if any command fails
They run as one unit with no other client's commands interleaving
They run in parallel across threads
They are retried automatically on failure

questions.explanation: EXEC runs the queued commands one after another with no interleaving from other clients — isolation. It does not provide rollback.

questions.prompt: During EXEC, one queued command errors because it targets the wrong type. What happens to the other commands?

options.text: They are all rolled back
They still execute — Redis has no rollback
EXEC refuses to run any command
They are queued again for a retry

questions.explanation: A run-time error in one command does not undo the others; Redis transactions have no rollback. Only a queuing-time error (before EXEC) aborts the whole transaction.

questions.prompt: Which statements about WATCH are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It provides optimistic locking (check-and-set)
If a watched key changes before EXEC, EXEC returns (nil)
It holds an exclusive lock on the key until EXEC
A (nil) result from EXEC means you should retry

questions.explanation: WATCH is optimistic (no lock is held); it aborts EXEC with (nil) if a watched key changed, signaling a retry. It does NOT take an exclusive lock.

questions.prompt: Why can't you read a value inside MULTI and branch on it before EXEC?

options.text: Reads are forbidden inside transactions
Queued commands don't return their values until EXEC runs them
MULTI encrypts all replies
Branching requires Redis Cluster

questions.explanation: Commands between MULTI and EXEC are only queued (they reply QUEUED), so their results aren't available to branch on. Use WATCH for check-and-set, or a Lua script to compute before writing.

questions.prompt: The command that abandons a queued transaction without executing anything is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: DISCARD throws away the queued commands and ends the transaction; nothing runs.

questions.prompt: For atomic read-compute-write logic that needs to branch before writing, what is often a better fit than MULTI/EXEC?

options.text: Pipelining
A Lua script or Redis Function (runs atomically and can make decisions)
Running the commands one at a time with no coordination
SUBSCRIBE

questions.explanation: A Lua script (or Redis Function) executes atomically as one uninterruptible unit and can read, decide, and write — cleaner than a transaction for conditional logic.
